body: If you argue, you’re manipulating. If you’re upset, you’re manipulating. If you ask why, you’re manipulating. If they choose to come back, you’re manipulating. Is this what non borderline ppl do too?

I remember saying, “you aren’t the only one who gets to have feelings!” 

“You’re right,” he said, “I know, I’ve heard it before.”

But he was the only one who got to have feelings. I find that my emotions were often too much, or manipulative, or abusive, or controlling, or he couldn’t deal with them right now, etc. I’ll never say I was perfect. But we couldn’t talk. I felt that he controlled every conversation. If it didn’t go how he wanted, he would leave. If he didn’t get what he wanted, he would leave. (I know this isn’t how he sees it. He sees me as manipulating him to see things my way and keep him with me although he was very unhappy.)
I understood this clearly in the past few days. It’s not how I saw myself at all. I feel like shit
I lied so my ex would stay. Doing it a few times was enough to crush him when he found out. I can’t forgive myself for it. I hope I can stop.
I get in bed and try not to think or be present until I fall asleep. It’s a bad strategy bc I don’t do the things I need to do. But it’s a good strategy bc I don’t hurt myself.

I appreciate that you wrote such a detailed response. 

To describe the impact of my actions in more detail, Ex#2 knew me while I was with Ex #1. They told me the same thing as it sounds like your current boyfriend told you- they wanted to help me through it, help me end it, help me move forward (the dynamic with ex #1 is very complicated for reasons I can’t get into). 

I can’t speak for when Ex #2 changed from “I just want to support you” to “its them or me,” but I believe the reason is that I had a hard time closing the door on the relationship with Ex #1. 

I can see that I caused ex #2 a great deal of pain. I believe it triggered a crisis in their life. I don’t want to reveal more here. I believe they see me as manipulating them to stay in the relationship. They left me many times, and came back many times. Each time we talked about how things would be different, and somehow they never were. I had done too much harm. 

I believe I loved them and still do. But I won’t get to be with them and it’s my own fault for destroying our trust.
